headline: Paper reports that language-model agents can organize context-learning loops from self-generated gameplay
summary: A November 17 preprint studies frozen language-model agents given a general goal to improve gameplay, basic tools for generating and testing games, and permission to edit text context. The authors report that newer models in three model families improve held-out gameplay without a prescribed optimization loop, and that one model's learned context transfers to different game settings and between model families. The experiments use small, controlled game benchmarks and report three teacher seeds per model; the paper does not establish open-ended or real-world recursive self-improvement, weight updates, or causal contribution of the observed learning strategies.
